note: Reference index for looking up what a sign might mean. Not a diagnosis. Every entry names its sources. breedRisk is only 'high' where the evidence genuinely names Giant Schnauzers or giant/deep-chested breeds.

conditions.name: Acute haemorrhagic diarrhoea syndrome (AHDS/HGE)
conditions.breedNote: Small and toy breeds including Miniature Schnauzers are over-represented; that risk is not documented in Giant Schnauzers.
signs: sudden bloody diarrhoea
diarrhoea like raspberry jam
vomiting and blood in the stool
gone flat very quickly
pale or tacky gums
won't eat at all
belly seems painful
collapsed or wobbly
went downhill in hours
conditions.whatToDo: Emergency — profuse bloody diarrhoea with lethargy can cause life-threatening fluid loss within hours. Go to a vet or emergency clinic immediately for IV fluids. Do not wait it out.

conditions.name: Acute kidney injury
signs: suddenly stopped eating
vomiting repeatedly
drinking loads then barely weeing
hardly any wee at all
very flat and weak
breath smells odd or chemical
wobbly on her legs
sore mouth or ulcers
got into antifreeze, grapes, raisins or lily plants
conditions.whatToDo: Go to a vet immediately and say what she may have eaten or been given — some causes such as antifreeze and grapes have a very short treatment window. Take the packaging or plant with you.

conditions.name: Acute pancreatitis
conditions.breedNote: The well-documented pancreatitis risk in Miniature Schnauzers belongs to that separate breed and does not transfer to Giant Schnauzers.
signs: vomiting over and over
praying position with front legs down and bottom up
hunched and won't straighten up
cries when i touch her belly
she got into fatty scraps or grease
won't eat and gone very quiet
greasy yellow diarrhoea
shivering and feels hot
drooling and lip smacking
conditions.whatToDo: Have her seen the same day, and go to an ER immediately if she is collapsing, retching without producing, or her belly is swelling — those signs cannot be told apart from bloat at home. Withhold food until a vet advises and give no human painkillers.

conditions.name: Anaphylaxis (severe allergic reaction)
signs: sudden vomiting and diarrhoea minutes after a sting, drug or vaccine
diarrhoea with blood in it
drooling heavily all of a sudden
swollen muzzle, eyelids or lips
raised itchy welts or hives over the body
gums going pale and legs feeling cold
sudden weakness or collapse
struggling to breathe
conditions.whatToDo: Go to an emergency vet immediately and say what she was exposed to and when. In dogs the liver, not the lungs, is the main shock organ, so severe anaphylaxis often looks like sudden vomiting, bloody diarrhoea and collapse rather than the wheezing people expect — normal-looking breathing does not mean she is fine.

conditions.name: Antifreeze poisoning
signs: found licking a puddle in the garage or driveway
wobbly like she's drunk
drinking and peeing a lot
vomiting
drooling
seems to sober up and look better after a few hours
very fast breathing the next day
peeing very little or not at all
very quiet, flat and cold
seizures
conditions.whatToDo: One of the most time-critical poisons there is — the antidote must start within hours. Drive to an emergency vet immediately on suspicion alone, and even if she seems to recover. Call ASPCA Animal Poison Control on 888-426-4435 or Pet Poison Helpline on 855-764-7661 from the car.

conditions.name: Bleeding that won't stop
signs: bleeding that won't stop after 5 minutes of firm pressure
blood spurting or pumping from a wound
blood soaking through dressing after dressing
nosebleed that keeps going
coughing up or vomiting blood
black tarry stool or fresh blood in stool
belly swelling up with pale gums and no wound to see
big spreading bruises under the skin
conditions.whatToDo: Press firmly with a clean cloth and hold for at least 5 minutes without lifting to peek; add layers rather than removing soaked ones. Do not use a tourniquet unless a vet on the phone tells you to. Internal bleeding shows no blood at all — pale gums, weakness and a swelling belly after trauma is an emergency even if she looks intact.

conditions.name: Cannabis or THC poisoning
signs: found an edible, a gummy or a joint end
wobbly, rocking on her feet
dribbling urine without meaning to
startles at sounds or touch
glazed eyes with wide pupils
very dull, sleepy and hard to rouse
drooling
slow heartbeat
cold to the touch
head bobbing or tremors
conditions.whatToDo: Most dogs recover with supportive care, but she still needs a vet — and edibles often also contain chocolate, raisins or xylitol, which are far more dangerous than the THC. Be honest with the vet about what she ate so she is treated correctly. Call ASPCA Animal Poison Control on 888-426-4435.

conditions.name: Checking her gums
signs: gums are pale, white or washed out
gums look blue, purple or muddy grey
gums are yellow, or the whites of her eyes look yellow
gums are dark brick red
colour takes more than 2 seconds to come back after you press
gums feel dry and tacky instead of slick
tiny red pinpoint dots or bruise patches on the gums
cold at the ears and paws with pale gums
conditions.whatToDo: Lift her lip, press the pink gum above a canine tooth until it blanches, release, and count how long the colour takes to come back. Normal is pink and under 2 seconds. Pale, white, blue, grey, yellow or brick-red gums, or a refill over 2 seconds, means go now. Normal pink gums do not rule out internal bleeding or early shock.
sources: UC Davis CVET normal vital signs — https://cvet.vetmed.ucdavis.edu/sites/g/files/dgvnsk13661/files/inline-files/CVET%20Vital%20Signs%2006_2024.pdf

conditions.name: Chocolate poisoning
signs: chewed wrappers or foil on the floor
vomiting, sometimes smelling of chocolate
diarrhoea
restless and can't settle
drinking and peeing more than usual
racing heart you can feel through her chest
panting and hot to the touch
muscle twitching or trembling
seizures
conditions.whatToDo: Call your vet or emergency clinic straight away, and phone ASPCA Animal Poison Control on 888-426-4435 or Pet Poison Helpline on 855-764-7661 with the wrapper, the type of chocolate and her weight in front of you. Do not induce vomiting unless a vet or poison line tells you to.

conditions.name: Congestive heart failure
conditions.breedNote: Not breed-specific in itself, but it is the usual end point of DCM, to which this breed is predisposed.
signs: breathing fast or hard at rest
more than 30 breaths a minute while asleep
coughing, worse at night or after lying down
gums or tongue look blue, grey or very pale
belly swollen and firm
sitting up with elbows out to breathe
collapsed or fainted
won't lie down or sleep
coughing up pink froth
conditions.whatToDo: An emergency — go straight to a vet and keep her cool, calm and carried rather than walked. Once stable, a sleeping breathing-rate count at home is the single most useful thing to track between visits.

conditions.name: Corneal ulcer
signs: holding the eye shut
squinting and watering
rubbing the eye with a paw
rubbing her face along the carpet
dull or pitted spot on the surface
cloudy or hazy patch on the eye
eye looks jelly-like or gooey
very sensitive to bright light
green or yellow discharge
came on after a walk in long grass
conditions.whatToDo: See a vet the same day for a fluorescein dye test — a deep or infected ulcer can melt through the cornea and rupture the eye within a day or two. Never use leftover or human steroid eye drops; steroids stop an ulcer healing and can make it perforate. Fit a cone to stop further rubbing on the way.

conditions.name: Distemper
conditions.breedNote: Not breed-linked. The vaccine series is not considered protective until the last dose at 16 weeks or older.
signs: goopy yellow-green gunk in both eyes
thick snotty nose and sneezing
hot, off food, and sleeping all day
coughing and rattly breathing
vomiting and watery diarrhoea
crusty nose and thickened, cracked paw pads
twitching in the face or one leg that won't stop
chewing-gum jaw movements
wobbly, drunk-looking walking
circling or pressing her head into the wall
conditions.whatToDo: Go in today, and the same hour if there is twitching, wobbliness or a seizure. Phone ahead — distemper is airborne and she must not sit in the lobby. Neurological signs can follow weeks later even after she seems to recover.

conditions.name: Fluid around the lungs
signs: fast shallow breathing with almost no cough
belly and chest moving in opposite directions with each breath
won't lie down flat, only sits or stands
stretching her neck out to breathe
elbows held out from her body
blue or grey gums
breathing hard but the cough is missing
suddenly quiet, weak or off her food
open-mouth breathing at rest
conditions.whatToDo: A go-now emergency: fluid around the lungs stops them expanding and often needs draining with a needle before anything else. Carry her, keep the car cool and quiet, and call ahead so the clinic can meet you with oxygen.

conditions.name: Gastric dilatation-volvulus (GDV)
conditions.breedNote: Giant, deep-chested breeds carry the highest documented GDV risk, and having a first-degree relative that bloated raises it further.
signs: retching with nothing coming up
swollen hard belly
belly tight like a drum
pacing and can't settle
drooling a lot all of a sudden
trying to vomit but only foam comes out
standing with elbows out and back arched
keeps turning to look at her side
panting and restless soon after eating
pale or grey gums
weak wobbly legs with a racing heart
collapsed suddenly
conditions.whatToDo: A true drop-everything emergency. Drive to the nearest 24-hour vet immediately and phone ahead so they can prepare. Do not wait to see if it passes, give nothing by mouth, and do not try home remedies.

conditions.name: Gastrointestinal foreign body obstruction
signs: throwing up every time she eats or drinks
vomiting yellow bile over and over
hasn't pooped in days
she ate a sock or a chunk of toy
won't eat and just lies there
belly hurts when i lift her
hunched up and tense
string or thread hanging from her mouth or bottom
straining and only passing liquid
getting more lethargic each day
conditions.whatToDo: Go to a vet today — an obstruction can kill bowel tissue within hours, and swallowed string is especially dangerous. Never pull on a string you can see, and never give a laxative or induce vomiting unless a vet tells you to.

conditions.name: Glaucoma
conditions.breedNote: VCA lists the Giant Schnauzer among breeds associated with glaucoma. No prevalence figures exist.
signs: eye looks bigger than the other
eye is bulging
white of the eye is very red
cornea looks cloudy or bluish
pupil is wide and won't shrink in light
squinting and rubbing at the eye
eye feels hard to the touch
suddenly can't see on that side
off her food and hiding
conditions.whatToDo: Go to a vet or emergency clinic now, tonight, not tomorrow — pressure this high blinds an eye within hours and is severely painful. Ask specifically that they measure intraocular pressure in both eyes, since the second eye is often at risk too.

conditions.name: Go to an emergency vet now
signs: gums are white, grey, blue or bright brick red
collapsed, won't stand, or can't get up
breathing hard, fast or open-mouthed at rest
trying to vomit but nothing comes up
belly is hard, swollen or drum-tight
bleeding that won't stop after 5 minutes of pressure
seizure, or more than one seizure in a day
unresponsive, dazed, or won't wake up properly
hit by a car, big fall, or attacked by another dog
straining to pee and nothing comes out
screaming, panting and can't settle at all
swollen face and hives within minutes of a sting or vaccine
temperature under 99F (37.2C) or over 104F (40C)
you think something is badly wrong even if you can't say why
conditions.whatToDo: Call the nearest 24-hour hospital, say you are on the way, and go now. Her normal numbers: temperature 101-102.5F (38.3-39.2C), resting heart rate 70-120 bpm, resting breathing 18-34 a minute, gums pink with colour returning in under 2 seconds. A dog can have completely normal-looking vitals and still be in serious trouble — never let a normal reading talk you out of going in.

conditions.name: Grapes, raisins and sultanas
signs: raisin box, trail mix or fruit cake torn open
vomiting within a few hours of eating grapes
diarrhoea
off her food
very quiet and flat
belly pain, standing hunched
drinking a lot and then barely peeing
peeing much less than normal, or not at all
weak and shaky a day or two later
conditions.whatToDo: There is no known safe amount — treat any ingestion as an emergency and get her seen the same day for decontamination and fluids. Call ASPCA Animal Poison Control on 888-426-4435 or Pet Poison Helpline on 855-764-7661. Do not induce vomiting unless told to.

conditions.name: Haemangiosarcoma
conditions.breedNote: No Giant Schnauzer link found — the UK pathology registry named German Shepherds, Mastiffs and Bullmastiffs.
signs: sudden weakness and pale gums
collapsed then seemed to recover
belly looks swollen or drooped
breathing fast for no reason
gums look white or grey
suddenly won't get up
wobbly back end
a soft blood-blister lump on the skin
conditions.whatToDo: Collapse with pale gums is a go-now emergency even if she picks up again within minutes — a bleeding spleen can stop and restart before bleeding fatally. Phone the emergency vet on the way rather than waiting to see if she improves.
sources: Rodriguez et al., SAVSNET, Vet Comp Oncol 2026 — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41736492/

conditions.name: Head injury
signs: hit by a car, kicked, or fell hard
bleeding from her nose, ears or mouth
one pupil bigger than the other
dazed, glazed over or won't wake up
circling or pressing her head into the wall
a seizure after a bang to the head
suddenly blind and bumping into things
staggering or falling to one side
vomiting after the injury
conditions.whatToDo: Go to an emergency vet immediately, keeping her as still as possible with her head slightly higher than her heart. Avoid anything pressing on her neck — no collar, no lead pressure — and never give human painkillers.

conditions.name: Heat stroke
conditions.breedNote: Raised heat-illness odds are documented in giant and double-coated breeds and in dogs heavier than average. Black coat colour itself is NOT supported — black and yellow Labradors showed no difference in body temperature.
signs: panting frantically and won't stop
bright red or brick-coloured gums
drooling thick ropey saliva
wobbly on her feet in the heat
collapsed after a walk on a warm day
hot to the touch through the coat
vomiting or bloody diarrhoea after exertion
glazed eyes, not responding to her name
seizure or twitching after overheating
conditions.whatToDo: Cool her FIRST, then travel. Pour or hose cold water over her whole body continuously, or immerse a fit adult dog in cold water, and keep air moving over her while someone phones the vet. Do NOT drape her in wet towels or blankets, do not use ice packs, and do not delay cooling in order to drive to the clinic.
sources: RVC VetCompass, cool first transport second — https://www.rvc.ac.uk/vetcompass/news/the-rvc-urges-owners-of-hot-dogs-to-cool-first-transport-second
Risk factors for severe and fatal heat-related illness, Animals 2022 — https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9144152/

conditions.name: Hit by a car, a fall, or a dog fight
signs: won't put weight on a leg after an accident
pale white gums
breathing fast, shallow or with effort
puncture holes in the skin after a scuffle
swelling under the skin that crackles
blood in her urine
belly looks tight or she flinches when touched
limb hanging at a strange angle
seems fine but is hiding away and shivering
conditions.whatToDo: Treat every road accident, fall or fight as an emergency even if she looks fine — internal bleeding, chest injury and deep bite damage often show up hours later. Cover open wounds with a clean cloth, apply gentle pressure to bleeding, move her on a flat rigid surface if she can't walk, and go straight to a vet.

conditions.name: Human painkiller poisoning
signs: chewed pill bottle or blister pack
vomiting, sometimes with blood or coffee-ground bits
black tarry poo
off her food
belly pain, hunched or stretching front-down
pale gums
brown or muddy-looking gums
swollen face, muzzle or paws
peeing much less than normal
wobbly or disoriented
seizures
conditions.whatToDo: Even one or two human tablets can burn holes in the gut, damage the kidneys, or destroy red blood cells. Go to a vet now with the packet and count what is missing. Call ASPCA Animal Poison Control on 888-426-4435 or Pet Poison Helpline on 855-764-7661. Never give a dog human painkillers.

conditions.name: Hypothermia
conditions.breedNote: Her dense harsh double coat is genuinely insulating, but that protection largely disappears once the coat is soaked through or clipped short.
signs: shivering that won't stop
ears, feet and tail feel icy
very sleepy and hard to rouse
stiff, slow, clumsy movement
pale or greyish gums
breathing slow and shallow
stops shivering but stays cold and floppy
collapsed after being wet and cold outdoors
conditions.whatToDo: Dry her thoroughly, wrap her in warmed blankets, move her somewhere warm and call the vet — a dog who has stopped shivering and gone floppy is an emergency. Do not use hairdryers, heat pads or hot water directly on her, and give nothing by mouth.

conditions.name: Immune-mediated haemolytic anaemia (IMHA)
conditions.breedNote: No established Giant Schnauzer predisposition, but middle-aged female dogs are over-represented in reported cases.
signs: gums look white, pale or yellow
whites of the eyes look yellow
urine looks orange, brown or like tea
very tired, sleeping all day
collapsed or won't get up
breathing fast without exercising
heart pounding fast at rest
off her food
recently unwell or on a new medicine
conditions.whatToDo: Go to an emergency vet now and ask for a PCV, blood smear, saline agglutination and Coombs test — this needs immunosuppressive treatment and often a transfusion, and delay costs lives. Bring a list of every medication, supplement, vaccine and tick exposure in the last month.
sources: ACVIM consensus statement on IMHA diagnosis, JVIM 2019 — https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/jvim.15441

conditions.name: Infectious canine hepatitis
conditions.breedNote: Dogs under one year are hit hardest, and unvaccinated puppies can die within hours of the first signs.
signs: sudden fever and won't get up
stopped eating and looks miserable
yellow gums or yellow whites of the eyes
belly swollen and sore to touch
vomiting and diarrhoea, sometimes bloody
swollen glands under the jaw
tiny bruises or bleeding from the gums
one or both eyes turn cloudy blue
swollen face, neck or legs
conditions.whatToDo: Yellow gums, a painful belly or any bruising in an unvaccinated puppy is a same-hour emergency. Signs appear 2-5 days after exposure, and the milky-blue 'hepatitis eye' shows up 1-2 weeks in, sometimes as the only clue after a mild illness.

conditions.name: Insect sting
signs: face swelling up
muzzle or eyes puffy within minutes
pawing at her face or mouth
raised lumpy bumps all over her
sudden intense itching
chewing at one foot after being in the grass
wheezing or struggling to breathe
collapse within half an hour of a sting
conditions.whatToDo: Scrape a bee sting out sideways with a card rather than squeezing it with tweezers, and apply something cool. Any facial or throat swelling, breathing difficulty, pale gums, vomiting or collapse is anaphylaxis — go straight to the vet. Never give human antihistamines without a dose from your vet.

conditions.name: Intervertebral disc disease
conditions.breedNote: Large breeds like hers typically get the slower type II disc protrusion after about age 5, rather than the sudden dachshund-type rupture.
signs: sudden yelp then won't move
hunched back and tense belly
trembling and can't get comfortable
won't jump into the car or onto the sofa
dragging one or both back feet
knuckling over onto the tops of her paws
back legs give out under her
holds her head low and won't look up
can't pee, or urine just dribbles out
conditions.whatToDo: Stop all exercise and confine her to a small quiet space; if you must move her, support her whole spine. Go to an emergency vet straight away if she cannot stand, has no feeling in her back feet, or cannot urinate — the window for surgery is measured in hours.

conditions.name: Intussusception
signs: vomiting that won't stop
bloody jelly-like diarrhoea
poop like raspberry jam
firm sausage-shaped lump in her belly
straining to poop with nothing coming out
started with diarrhoea and now she won't eat
belly pain and hunched back
getting weaker by the hour
something red poking out of her bottom
conditions.whatToDo: Get to a vet or emergency clinic now — the trapped bowel loses its blood supply and this usually needs surgery. Bring a photo or sample of any bloody stool.

conditions.name: Laryngeal paralysis
conditions.breedNote: Documented in middle-aged to older large and giant breeds. The best-documented breeds are Labradors, Irish Setters and Great Danes; Giant Schnauzers sit in the size group but are not named.
signs: noisy raspy breathing in, like a snore while awake
her bark sounds hoarse or has changed
loud harsh breathing that gets worse in heat
gets winded and loud on short walks
gagging or coughing when she eats or drinks
stretching her neck out to breathe
panting hard and can't settle
blue or grey gums, or collapse in warm weather
hind legs seem weaker or she scuffs her back feet
conditions.whatToDo: If she is in noisy respiratory distress, overheated, or has blue or grey gums, go to an emergency vet now, keep her cool and calm, and do not muzzle or restrain her neck. For milder noisy breathing or a changed bark, book an exam soon and keep her cool and harness-walked.

conditions.name: Leptospirosis
conditions.breedNote: Lepto is not always given at the first puppy visit — confirm whether her series includes it before assuming she is covered. It spreads to people.
signs: fever, then suddenly flat and sore all over
drinking and peeing far more than usual
then barely peeing at all
vomiting and refusing food
yellow gums, eyes or skin
dark orange or brown pee
stiff, hunched, painful when handled
red, bloodshot eyes
drank from a puddle, pond or ditch a few days ago
conditions.whatToDo: Go the same hour if she is vomiting, yellow, or has changed how much she pees — lepto kidney failure moves fast and is treatable with prompt antibiotics and fluids. Signs begin about 4-12 days after contact with infected urine or water. Wear gloves for urine cleanup.

conditions.name: Parvovirus
conditions.breedNote: No breed link. Being 9 weeks old and mid-series is the real risk factor — maternal antibody is fading but vaccine protection is not yet complete.
signs: won't eat and is flat
vomiting over and over
bloody diarrhoea with an awful smell
watery brown diarrhoea that soaks the bedding
went from playful to limp in a day
belly hurts when you pick her up
gums look pale, dry or tacky
cold ears and paws, shivering
skin stays tented when you pinch it
no interest in her favourite food or toy
conditions.whatToDo: A same-hour emergency in a puppy mid-series — go now, and phone ahead so they can meet you outside and keep her out of the waiting room. Signs start 5-7 days after exposure and she can shed virus 4-5 days before looking sick, so isolate her and disinfect with dilute bleach.

conditions.name: Pericardial effusion
conditions.breedNote: Documented as a large- and giant-breed problem generally rather than in Giant Schnauzers specifically.
signs: belly swollen and getting bigger
suddenly very weak or wobbly
gums look white or muddy
collapsed
breathing fast and shallow
very quiet and cold to touch
retching or a soft cough
off food and hiding away
seems fine one hour, crashing the next
conditions.whatToDo: Go to an emergency vet immediately and ask for a point-of-care ultrasound of the heart — draining the fluid can be lifesaving within minutes. Do not let her walk in.

conditions.name: Pneumonia
conditions.breedNote: Aspiration risk rises with laryngeal paralysis or megaoesophagus, both documented in large-breed dogs, and after anaesthesia or repeated vomiting.
signs: wet rattly cough
breathing fast even when resting
belly heaving with each breath
fever, hot ears, shivering
won't eat and won't get up
stretching her neck out to breathe
elbows held out from her body
blue or grey gums
green or yellow gunk from her nose
coughing that started right after vomiting or choking
conditions.whatToDo: Go to a vet or emergency clinic now if she is breathing fast or hard at rest — pneumonia worsens quickly and often needs chest x-rays, oxygen and antibiotics. Keep her cool and quiet in the car and do not make her walk in.

conditions.name: Poisonous plants
signs: chewed leaves, or a dug-up seed, nut or bulb
vomiting, sometimes with blood
black tarry poo
drooling
off her food
very quiet and flat
yellow tinge to gums or eyes
wobbly or trembling
slow or irregular heartbeat
seizures
conditions.whatToDo: Photograph or bag the plant, then call a vet the same day — sago palm seeds cause liver failure and azalea or lily-of-the-valley can slow the heart dangerously. Call ASPCA Animal Poison Control on 888-426-4435 or Pet Poison Helpline on 855-764-7661 for plant identification.

conditions.name: Pyometra (womb infection)
conditions.breedNote: No Giant Schnauzer figure exists, but around 1 in 4 entire bitches develop pyometra by age 10 in Swedish insurance data. She will be entire until at least 24 months.
signs: pus or smelly discharge from her vulva, often weeks after a season
drinking loads and weeing far more than usual
off her food and very flat, four to eight weeks after a season
swollen, tight or painful belly
vomiting or runny poo
licking her private parts constantly
panting, shivery or feels hot
pale gums, wobbly or collapsing
no discharge at all but getting sicker by the hour
conditions.whatToDo: Treat any unspayed bitch who is unwell within about two months of a season as pyometra until a vet rules it out, and phone the emergency vet now rather than waiting for morning. Closed pyometra produces no discharge at all and deteriorates fastest — absence of discharge is not reassurance.

conditions.name: Rabies exposure
conditions.breedNote: A 9-week-old is normally too young for the rabies vaccine (usually 12-16 weeks), so any bite from a wild animal or unknown dog is treated as an exposure.
signs: bitten, scratched or found mouthing a bat, raccoon or stray
chewing or licking at one spot on her body
personality flipped, clingy puppy now hiding or snappy
snapping at the air
drooling a lot and dropping food
jaw hangs open and she can't swallow
bark or cry sounds different
restless pacing, spooked by light and noise
wobbly or dragging back legs
conditions.whatToDo: Any bat contact or bite from a wild, stray or unknown-vaccination animal is a same-hour call to your vet and your local health department, even with no symptoms. Do not destroy the biting animal's head if it can be tested. Once signs appear rabies is essentially always fatal — handle her with gloves.

conditions.name: Rat and mouse bait poisoning
signs: green, blue or pink pellets or blocks found chewed
bruising under the skin
bleeding gums
nosebleed
coughing or wheezing
breathing fast or with effort
pale gums
sudden weakness or collapse
blood in her pee or poo
tired and won't walk like she used to
conditions.whatToDo: Signs are often delayed 3 to 7 days, so call the vet the moment you suspect she got into bait rather than waiting for bleeding. Take the packet so the exact chemical can be identified. Call ASPCA Animal Poison Control on 888-426-4435 or Pet Poison Helpline on 855-764-7661.

conditions.name: Ruptured splenic mass (bleeding into the belly)
conditions.breedNote: Large breeds over about eight years old are at elevated risk for splenic masses; Giant Schnauzers are not separately named in the published breed data.
signs: collapsed then got up like nothing happened
white or grey gums
suddenly very weak in the back legs
belly swelling but no retching
belly feels full of fluid
cold ears and paws
breathing fast and shallow
wobbly and fainting
quiet and off food for days then crashed
conditions.whatToDo: Emergency. A dog who collapses then seems to recover is still bleeding inside. Go straight to an ER, carry her rather than letting her walk, and keep her quiet in the car.

conditions.name: Seizure (happening now)
conditions.breedNote: Idiopathic epilepsy is a documented Giant Schnauzer concern, so a seizure in this breed is not a rare event.
signs: collapsed and paddling on her side
stiff legs and jerking all over
chomping or chewing at nothing
drooling or foaming at the mouth
peed or pooped herself during it
eyes open but glassy and not there
another one before she has recovered
won't wake up properly afterwards
dazed, pacing and bumping into things after
conditions.whatToDo: Keep your hands away from her mouth — she cannot swallow her tongue. Move furniture and other pets clear, dim the lights, note the start time and film it if you can. Go to an emergency vet if it passes 5 minutes, if she has more than one in 24 hours, or if she does not fully come round between them.
sources: ACVIM consensus on status epilepticus, JVIM 2024 — https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/jvim.16928

conditions.name: Shock
signs: gums pale, white or grey
capillary refill slower than 2 seconds
racing heart, over 180 beats a minute
pulse feels weak or you can't find it
ears, paws and legs feel cold
shivering or body temperature dropping
breathing fast and shallow
dull, glazed or not responding
weak, wobbly or collapsed
conditions.whatToDo: Immediate emergency. Keep her warm with a blanket, minimise handling, give nothing by mouth, and drive straight to a 24-hour hospital while someone phones ahead. Go on the pattern — weakness plus cold extremities plus a racing heart — even if individual numbers look borderline.

conditions.name: Slug and snail bait poisoning
signs: blue, green or brown pellets in her mouth, poo or vomit
shaking and restless
tremors running through her whole body
very hot to the touch
drooling heavily
wobbly and uncoordinated
twitchy, startles at everything
vomiting
fast, heavy breathing
seizures
conditions.whatToDo: Signs can start within minutes and the tremors and overheating can kill quickly — drive straight to an emergency vet rather than watching at home. Call ASPCA Animal Poison Control on 888-426-4435. Do not induce vomiting once she is tremoring.

conditions.name: Snake bite
signs: sudden yelp and swelling on the face or leg
two small puncture marks with oozing
rapid dark swelling spreading from the bite
bruising around the bite area
shaky and weak within the hour
drooling heavily and vomiting
wobbly back end or unable to stand
pale gums and racing heart
conditions.whatToDo: Keep her as still and quiet as possible, carry her rather than letting her walk, and get to a vet immediately — antivenom works best in the first few hours. Do not apply a tourniquet, do not cut or suck the wound, and do not use ice.

conditions.name: Something stuck in her mouth or throat
signs: pawing at her mouth
gagging or retching
sudden heavy drooling
won't close her mouth
bone or stick wedged across the roof of the mouth
object caught between two teeth
bleeding from the mouth
coughing or choking after chewing a stick
swelling under the jaw or throat
fever a few days after a stick chase
conditions.whatToDo: An emergency — go in now. Do not try to dig an object out with fingers or pliers; you can push it deeper or be bitten. Stick and bone injuries can leave splinters that migrate and abscess days later, so mention any recent stick chewing even if the mouth looks clear.

conditions.name: Splenic torsion
conditions.breedNote: Large, deep-chested breeds are over-represented, and it can occur alongside or after bloat.
signs: on-and-off vomiting for a few days
belly slowly getting bigger
pale gums
dark red or brown pee
weak and off her food
swollen painful belly on the left side
restless and can't get comfortable
fast breathing and racing heart
seems fine one hour then crashes the next
collapsed
conditions.whatToDo: Go to an emergency vet now — a twisted spleen can look like a vague slow illness for days then turn into shock without warning. Mention any past bloat episode.

conditions.name: Sudden blindness
conditions.breedNote: Females are affected by SARDS more often than males; among schnauzers it is the Miniature, not the Giant, that is over-represented.
signs: walked into a wall out of nowhere
blind within days
pupils wide open and not reacting to light
startles when you approach
pacing or disoriented indoors
eye looks completely normal but she can't see
suddenly ravenous
drinking and peeing a lot more
put on weight quickly
conditions.whatToDo: Get her seen urgently — sudden blindness can mean glaucoma, retinal detachment, high blood pressure or a brain problem, several of which are treatable if caught within hours. If the eyes look normal, ask about an electroretinogram and bloodwork for Cushing's.

conditions.name: Urinary obstruction (blocked bladder)
signs: straining hard and nothing comes out
crying or yelping when she tries
going into position over and over
belly hard, swollen and painful
vomiting and off her food
gone quiet, flat and weak
hasn't weed at all today
only a few bloody drops
collapsed or wobbly
conditions.whatToDo: A genuine emergency — go to a vet or out-of-hours clinic straight away, day or night. A bladder that cannot empty causes kidney damage and dangerous potassium build-up within a day, and it can be fatal.

conditions.name: Xylitol poisoning
signs: chewed sugar-free gum, mints or a peanut butter jar
sudden collapse after eating gum
wobbly like she's drunk
weak and dull within an hour
vomiting
trembling or shaking
seizures
hard to rouse
yellow tinge to gums or eyes a day or two later
conditions.whatToDo: This drops blood sugar within 10 to 60 minutes and can damage the liver a day later, so go to a vet now even if she looks fine. Call ASPCA Animal Poison Control on 888-426-4435 or Pet Poison Helpline on 855-764-7661 on the way. Never give anything by mouth if she is already wobbly or seizing.

conditions.name: Addison's disease
conditions.breedNote: Not a listed predisposed breed, though young to middle-aged females are over-represented overall.
signs: on and off vomiting or diarrhoea
picky, going off her food
losing weight slowly
flat and weak, better then worse again
shivering or trembling
wobbly on her legs
drinking and weeing more
always crashes after stress like boarding or travel
black tarry stool
collapse with a slow heart rate
conditions.whatToDo: Get her seen the same day for bloods including electrolytes, and specifically ask about Addison's if she has a history of vague illness that keeps returning. Collapse with a slow heart rate is an emergency needing IV fluids within hours.

conditions.name: Aural haematoma (swollen ear flap)
signs: ear flap swollen up like a pillow or water balloon
the flap feels squishy, warm and heavy
she cries when you touch the ear flap
the swelling came up over a few hours
days of head shaking just before the swelling
the ear droops or flops to one side
on a cropped ear, the standing ear suddenly sags
the flap looks bruised or purple inside
conditions.whatToDo: Get her in the same day — haematomas are painful, and left alone the flap scars down into a shrunken shape that can narrow the ear canal. The vet must also treat whatever made her shake her head, or it will fill again.

conditions.name: Bacterial ear infection with pus
signs: yellow, green or creamy pus in the ear
a rotten smell you can smell across the room
she screams or snaps when the ear is touched
raw, ulcerated skin inside the ear
blood-tinged discharge
the ear canal looks swollen almost shut
she holds her head down and to one side
she goes off her food and seems miserable
the ear has got dramatically worse in a day or two
conditions.whatToDo: Get her seen the same day — painful, pus-filled ears can involve resistant bacteria and can track toward the middle ear. Do not flush or medicate at home; some ear medications are harmful if the eardrum has ruptured.

conditions.name: Bladder stones
conditions.breedNote: It is the Miniature Schnauzer, not the Giant Schnauzer, that carries the documented calcium oxalate stone risk.
signs: straining and nothing much comes out
blood in her wee
squatting again and again
crying or whimpering when she wees
wee dribbles out in a thin stream
accidents in the house
belly seems tender when touched
gritty bits or sand in the wee
conditions.whatToDo: Get her seen the same day for imaging, because stones can move into the urethra and block urine flow. Some types dissolve on a prescription diet and others need removing, so the stone must be analysed.

conditions.name: Broken tooth
conditions.breedNote: Risk comes from size and bite force rather than genetics: large, powerful-jawed dogs break teeth more often on hard chews.
signs: broken or chipped tooth
sharp edge on a tooth
pink or black dot in the middle of a tooth
tooth looks grey or purple
bleeding from the mouth
chewing on one side
dropping food
yelping when she bites down
swelling under one eye
pawing at her face
conditions.whatToDo: A broken tooth with any pink, red or dark spot in the middle has an exposed nerve, is painful and will not heal — get it seen the same day. Prevention is the thumbnail rule: if you cannot dent a chew with your thumbnail, it can break a tooth. That rules out antlers, bones, hooves, dried yak chews, ice and rigid nylon.

conditions.name: Burned paw pads
signs: limping after hot pavement
licking or chewing her feet nonstop
pads look red, shiny or blistered
chunks of pad peeling away
won't put a foot down at all
refuses to walk on the path but fine on grass
yelps when you touch a paw
bloody paw prints on the floor
conditions.whatToDo: Cool the feet with cool running water, keep them clean and loosely covered, and stop her licking. Get her seen the same day — burned pads are painful, easily infected, and need proper pain relief rather than home creams.

conditions.name: Canine influenza
signs: cough that drags on for weeks
thick yellow or green nose discharge
fever and shivering
very tired, sleeping much more than usual
off her food
runny eyes
breathing faster than normal at rest
was recently around lots of other dogs
several dogs in the area are sick at once
conditions.whatToDo: Call the vet the same day and say you suspect flu so they can isolate her on arrival. Treat any fast or laboured breathing, blue or grey gums, or refusal to eat as an emergency, because a small share of dogs develop pneumonia.

conditions.name: Cruciate ligament rupture
conditions.breedNote: One of the most common orthopaedic disorders in dogs and heavier dogs are over-represented, but the Giant Schnauzer is not among the breeds identified as high-risk in the large prevalence work.
signs: sudden three-legged lameness on a back leg
toe-touching the ground with one hind leg
back leg lameness after twisting or skidding
sits with the sore leg stuck out sideways
swelling on the inside of the knee
clicking from the knee when she walks
won't push off that leg going upstairs
thigh muscle shrinking on one side
conditions.whatToDo: Have her examined promptly — the knee needs hands-on stability testing and often sedated radiographs, and a big dog with a torn cruciate usually does best with surgery. Crate rest and lead-only movement until she is seen.

conditions.name: Dehydration
signs: skin on the shoulders stays tented when you lift and let go
gums feel dry, sticky or tacky rather than wet
eyes look sunken or dull
hasn't drunk anything for most of a day
vomiting or diarrhoea that keeps going
urine looks dark and strong-smelling
flat, tired and slow to get up
conditions.whatToDo: Lift the loose skin over her shoulder blades and let go — it should snap flat almost instantly. Skin that stays tented, tacky gums or sunken eyes mean a vet the same day, not just a bowl of water. The skin tent is crude and reads falsely normal in young or overweight dogs.

conditions.name: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM)
conditions.breedNote: Giant Schnauzers are a recognised DCM breed, and an RBM20 variant associated with DCM has been found in Giant and Standard Schnauzers. The evidence base is small — treat as suggestive rather than settled.
signs: tiring quickly on walks
breathing fast while asleep
coughing, worse at night
belly looks swollen or drum-tight
fainted or wobbled and went down
off her food
losing weight or muscle over the topline
restless, won't settle at night
gums look pale or greyish
won't lie flat on her side
conditions.whatToDo: Get her seen within a day and ask specifically for an echocardiogram plus ECG. Count her breaths per minute while she is asleep and bring that number. Struggling to breathe, blue or white gums, or collapse is an emergency.
sources: Leach et al., J Vet Cardiol — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34144877/

conditions.name: Exercise intolerance
conditions.breedNote: Exercise, not hot cars, triggers the large majority of canine heat-related illness — so a big working dog encouraged to run in warm weather sits in the higher-exposure group.
signs: lags behind on walks she used to enjoy
sits or lies down and won't move on
panting hard long after stopping
wants to stop in every patch of shade
takes much longer than usual to settle
back legs go wobbly near the end of a run
gums look muddy or pale after exercise
off her food the evening after a big walk
conditions.whatToDo: Stop the exercise, get her into shade with cool water over her and air moving, and offer small drinks. Book a same-day check — repeated exercise intolerance can be early heat illness, pain, anaemia or heart disease rather than being unfit.

conditions.name: Fainting and irregular heartbeat
conditions.breedNote: Ventricular arrhythmias are documented in giant-breed DCM generally and can appear before the heart looks enlarged on ultrasound.
signs: fainted and got straight back up
went limp for a few seconds
stumbled or buckled during a walk
collapsed after excitement or barking
heartbeat feels irregular under the chest
sudden weakness then normal again
gums went white briefly
wobbly for a moment after standing up
conditions.whatToDo: Book a same-day exam with an ECG, and ask about a 24-hour Holter monitor since intermittent rhythm problems are easily missed on a short trace. Film any episode on your phone if you safely can — it helps tell fainting from a seizure.
sources: Wess et al., J Vet Cardiol 2017 — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28965673/

conditions.name: Frostbite
signs: ear tips or tail look pale, grey or bluish
skin feels cold and hard to the touch
she flinches when the area is touched
swelling once the area warms up
blisters on ears, tail or paws
skin turning black over the following days
limping after a long spell in snow
conditions.whatToDo: Move her somewhere warm and dry and apply warm — not hot — compresses that feel comfortable on your own hand, then pat dry and go to the vet. Never rub or massage the area, never use a hairdryer, and don't rewarm if she is going straight back out into the cold.

conditions.name: Growth plate injury
conditions.breedNote: Growth plates stay open longest in giant breeds, so her skeleton is vulnerable for longer than a small dog's.
signs: sudden severe limp right after a fall or jump
won't touch the foot down at all
swelling right at the wrist or just above the knee
leg looks bent or twisted compared to the other one
one front leg turning out more than it used to
cries when the leg near a joint is handled
a puppy limp that isn't better in 24 hours
paw rotating outward as she grows
conditions.whatToDo: Get her seen the same day and keep her confined — growth plate fractures look minor from the outside but can stop a bone growing and leave a permanently bent limb. Radiographs of both legs let the vet compare sides.

conditions.name: Hookworms
signs: pale or white gums
black tarry poop
bloody diarrhoea
weak and wobbly puppy
very tired, sleeps all the time
not gaining weight
dry brittle coat
itchy red paws or belly
fast breathing
sudden collapse
conditions.whatToDo: A young puppy with pale gums or black stools can be bleeding internally and needs seeing the same day, sometimes with a transfusion. Bring a stool sample; expect repeat deworming plus year-round prevention.

conditions.name: Hot spot (acute moist dermatitis)
conditions.breedNote: Thick double coats that stay damp after swimming, rain or bathing are a classic setup for hot spots.
signs: red raw patch that appeared overnight
oozing wet sore under the fur
she won't let me touch that spot
hair falling out around a wet patch
spot getting bigger by the hour
licking or chewing one place nonstop
smelly discharge on her cheek or hip
matted hair stuck over a wound
appeared after a swim or a bath
hot to the touch
conditions.whatToDo: Get her seen the same day — these spread fast and are painful, and the area usually needs clipping, cleaning and pain relief. Do not use human antiseptic creams or try to clip a painful spot yourself.

conditions.name: Hypertrophic osteodystrophy (HOD)
conditions.breedNote: A disorder of young, growing large- and giant-breed dogs. No Giant Schnauzer prevalence figure exists; breeds most often named are Weimaraner, Great Dane, Boxer and Irish Setter.
signs: hot, swollen, painful bands just above the wrists
both front legs sore at the same time
won't stand up or put weight on her legs
high fever with the limping
off her food and very flat
cries when you touch just above the paw joints
diarrhoea or a snotty nose alongside the lameness
comes on suddenly in a puppy under six months
conditions.whatToDo: Ring your vet the same day — unlike growing pains, HOD can make a puppy systemically ill and can permanently damage growth plates. She will need radiographs, pain relief and sometimes steroids.

conditions.name: Idiopathic epilepsy
conditions.breedNote: A pedigree analysis of 285 Giant Schnauzers estimated heritability at 0.78, with average onset around 3 years. The underlying figures come from conference proceedings rather than a peer-reviewed journal paper.
signs: seizures with no obvious trigger
first fit between six months and six years old
completely normal and healthy in between
several seizures bunched into the same day or week
restless, clingy or hiding just before one
wobbly, ravenous or confused for hours after
seizures mostly at night or while resting
staring spells or snapping at invisible flies
conditions.whatToDo: Book a vet workup after any first seizure and keep a written log of date, length and what she was doing — medication decisions are made on that pattern.
sources: ACVIM consensus on seizure management, JVIM 2016 — https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/jvim.13841

conditions.name: Inherited B12 (cobalamin) malabsorption
conditions.breedNote: Giant Schnauzers carry a breed-specific recessive AMN gene variant causing selective intestinal B12 malabsorption. A DNA test exists.
signs: puppy not growing properly
failure to thrive
picky and won't eat
unusually tired for a puppy
loose stool since weaning
pale gums
thin despite feeding well
wobbly or confused episodes
slow to put on weight
protein found in her urine
conditions.whatToDo: If a young Giant Schnauzer is failing to grow, off her food or lethargic, ask specifically for serum cobalamin, a blood count and a urine protein check. Confirmed cases respond very well to lifelong B12 injections, and parents and littermates can be DNA tested.

conditions.name: Lymphoma
conditions.breedNote: No established Giant Schnauzer predisposition; the breed appears in the literature only as isolated case reports.
signs: hard lumps under the jaw
swollen glands behind the knees
lumps on both sides of the neck
drinking and weeing much more
losing weight but still eating
off colour and tired
swollen face or muzzle
lumps that appeared over a week or two
conditions.whatToDo: Firm, painless, symmetrical lumps where the glands sit — under the jaw, in front of the shoulders, behind the knees — should be seen within a day or two for a needle sample. Lymphoma responds well to treatment but moves fast, so don't watch and wait.
sources: Rodriguez et al., SAVSNET, Vet Comp Oncol 2026 — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41736492/

conditions.name: Megaoesophagus
conditions.breedNote: Inherited congenital cases are documented in Miniature Schnauzers and some giant-breed families, but not in Giant Schnauzers.
signs: bringing food back up undigested
regurgitating without heaving
food comes up in a tube shape
coughing after eating or drinking
losing weight but hungry
bad breath
noisy or rattly breathing
runny nose after meals
conditions.whatToDo: Regurgitation (passive, no heaving) is different from vomiting and needs chest imaging plus tests for myasthenia gravis, Addison's and hypothyroidism. Any fever, cough or laboured breathing means aspiration pneumonia — go the same day.

conditions.name: Melanoma (mouth, toe or skin)
conditions.breedNote: A UK registry of over 1.1 million tumour records named the Giant Schnauzer among the three highest-risk breeds for melanoma, alongside Rottweilers and Shar Peis. The headline odds ratio is for that three-breed group, so it is not certainly this breed's own figure.
signs: dark lump in the mouth
bad breath that came on suddenly
drooling or blood-tinged saliva
dropping food while eating
a black lump on a toe
swollen toe with a dark mass
loose tooth with a lump beside it
face looks swollen on one side
black raised lump on the skin
a dark spot that is growing or spreading
conditions.whatToDo: Look in her mouth whenever you can, and treat any dark or ulcerated mass, or a black lump on a toe, as urgent — oral melanoma spreads early, so days matter. Ask for a biopsy and chest imaging rather than waiting to see whether it grows.
sources: Rodriguez et al., SAVSNET, Vet Comp Oncol 2026 — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41736492/

conditions.name: Middle and inner ear infection
signs: head tilted permanently to one side
stumbling, circling or falling over
eyes flicking side to side on their own
one side of her face droops
she cannot blink that eye properly
one pupil looks smaller and the eyelid droops
she cries when she opens her mouth
she does not respond to her name anymore
ear infections that keep coming back
dry, gunky eye on the same side as the sore ear
conditions.whatToDo: Call the vet today, and go to an emergency clinic if she is falling over, vomiting or cannot stand. Expect a deep ear exam under sedation and possibly imaging — the middle ear cannot be assessed properly in an awake dog.

conditions.name: Pyelonephritis (kidney infection)
signs: off her food and low in herself
feels hot and shivery
sore over her lower back
flinches when you touch her sides
drinking and weeing more
blood in her wee
sicky
a bladder infection that came back
hunched up and reluctant to move
conditions.whatToDo: Get her seen the same day with a urine sample — kidney infections need a urine culture and a longer antibiotic course than a simple bladder infection. Untreated they can permanently scar the kidneys.

conditions.name: Ticks and tick-borne disease
signs: limping that moves leg to leg
sore and stiff, hates being touched
fever and shivering
off food and low energy
swollen joints
swollen glands
walking like she's on eggshells
nosebleed or pinpoint bruising
found a tick attached
pale gums
conditions.whatToDo: Remove attached ticks promptly with tweezers at the skin line, steady and straight out, and note the date. Fever, shifting lameness, bruising or lethargy after tick exposure warrants a same-day visit and a blood test.

conditions.name: Vestibular disease
signs: head tilted to one side
eyes flicking rapidly side to side
falling or leaning to one side
walking in circles always the same way
rolling over and can't right herself
staggering like she's drunk
came on suddenly overnight
drooling, vomiting or car-sick looking
won't eat or won't stand up
conditions.whatToDo: Keep her on the floor away from stairs and hard furniture, put food and water within reach, and get her examined the same day — a vet needs to separate benign vestibular disease from an inner ear infection, stroke or brain tumour. Most idiopathic cases start improving within about 72 hours.

conditions.name: A lump that needs checking
aka: when to worry about a lump
conditions.breedNote: In a Swiss registry of 11,740 skin tumours across 227 breeds, the Giant Schnauzer had the highest skin tumour incidence of any breed, roughly four times the all-breed average.
signs: lump that's growing
a lump that changes size
lump that's hard and fixed in place
lump that bleeds or weeps
sore that won't heal
lump she won't stop licking
lump that's grown in under a month
lump that seems painful
losing weight alongside a lump
a lump you can't move under the skin
conditions.whatToDo: Given how tumour-prone this breed is, run a hands-on check monthly including every toe and her mouth, and write down where each lump is and how big it is. Book a needle sample for anything new, growing, hard, fixed, bleeding or non-healing — no vet can tell a benign lump from a malignant one by feel alone.
sources: Graf et al., Swiss Canine Cancer Registry, Vet Pathol 2018 — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30131007/

conditions.name: Atopic dermatitis (environmental allergy)
conditions.breedNote: No documented excess risk in Giant Schnauzers, but the harsh double coat hides early redness so it is often caught late.
signs: chewing her paws
licking her front legs raw
rubbing her face on the carpet
scratching her armpits and groin
red skin in the bald spots under her belly
head shaking and dark ear gunk
itch that comes back every spring
skin under the beard looks pink
hair thinning where she licks most
worse after walks in tall grass
conditions.whatToDo: Book a proper itch workup rather than cycling through shampoos — atopy is lifelong and needs a management plan plus year-round flea control. Ask about Cytopoint, Apoquel, ciclosporin, or allergy testing with immunotherapy if flares are frequent.

conditions.name: Chronic inflammatory enteropathy (IBD)
conditions.breedNote: Documented predispositions are in German Shepherds, Boxers, Yorkshire Terriers and Soft-Coated Wheaten Terriers, not Giant Schnauzers.
signs: soft stool for weeks
diarrhoea that keeps coming back
losing weight but still eating
vomiting on and off for months
mucus or slime on the stool
straining and small frequent poos
noisy gurgling gut
dull coat and low energy
swollen belly or puffy legs
conditions.whatToDo: Signs lasting more than three weeks need a workup — bloods, faecal tests, B12/folate, often imaging or biopsies. Keep a written diary of stool, food and weight, and ask about a therapeutic diet trial before steroids.
sources: ACVIM consensus statement, chronic inflammatory enteropathy — https://academic.oup.com/jvim/article/40/1/aalaf017/8429723

conditions.name: Chronic kidney disease
signs: drinking far more water than usual
weeing much more and bigger puddles
losing weight slowly
picky with food or off it altogether
coat looks dull and scruffy
sicky now and then
bad breath
tired, sleeping more, less keen on walks
occasional accidents overnight
pale gums
conditions.whatToDo: Book blood and urine tests including urine protein and blood pressure, and start measuring how much water she drinks in 24 hours. Kidney disease is managed rather than cured, and catching it early makes a real difference.

conditions.name: Coccidia
signs: watery diarrhoea in a young puppy
streaks of blood in loose stool
mucus jelly poop
started right after coming home
dehydrated, skin tents up
sunken eyes and dry gums
belly pain, hunched up
vomiting along with diarrhoea
weak and listless
conditions.whatToDo: Ask for a faecal test and treatment — routine dewormers do not kill coccidia. Go the same day instead if the puppy is limp, dry-gummed or vomiting, because puppies dehydrate fast.

conditions.name: Constipation
signs: straining but nothing comes out
hard dry pellet stools
hasn't pooed in two days
crying or hunching when straining
chalky white stool after eating bones
off her food and restless
vomiting with no bowel movement
swollen or firm belly
conditions.whatToDo: See a vet — straining can equally mean an obstruction, a prostate or pelvic problem, or colitis. Never give over-the-counter laxatives or mineral oil without veterinary direction. Straining plus retching or bloating is an emergency.

conditions.name: Cropped or posted ear problems
conditions.breedNote: Cropping is common in this breed for the standard look, but AAHA opposes it as a cosmetic procedure and it carries anaesthetic, wound and long-term aftercare costs the natural ear does not.
signs: redness, ooze or pus along the cut edge
a bad smell coming from the ear edge
the edge looks dark, dry or dying
stitches pulled out or gaping
raw skin or sores where the tape sits
swelling of the flap above the tape
the ear feels cold or the tip looks pale
she keeps scratching the posts off
the ear tip flops over and will not stand
conditions.whatToDo: Get pus, foul smell, dark or dying edges, or a fever checked the same day. Have looser problems seen within a few days by the vet managing the crop. Never leave a wrap on that is tight, wet or smelly, and do not re-tape over inflamed skin.

conditions.name: Cushing's disease
conditions.breedNote: No reported Giant Schnauzer predisposition; Poodles, Dachshunds, Boxers and small terriers are the over-represented breeds.
signs: drinking and weeing a lot
always ravenous, raiding bins
pot belly or sagging tummy
panting a lot even when resting
hair loss over the body but not the head or legs
thin skin that bruises or tears easily
muscle wasting over the back and back legs
cuts and grazes slow to heal
repeated urine infections
conditions.whatToDo: Book a non-urgent appointment and note how much she drinks in 24 hours. Screening starts with routine bloods and urine before a specific adrenal test. Declare any steroid creams, drops or tablets she has had — they invalidate the results.

conditions.name: Damp beard and matted-coat dermatitis
conditions.breedNote: A permanently damp beard plus harsh furnishings that mat behind the ears, in the armpits and on the legs make this the breed's most predictable skin problem.
signs: beard smells sour
beard stays wet after every drink
pink or brown staining on her chin hair
red bumpy skin under the beard
matted behind the ears
mats in her armpits and back legs
flinches when I brush her furnishings
sore red skin found under a mat
smells musty even after a bath
crusty skin along her lip folds
conditions.whatToDo: Have painful or tight mats clipped out professionally rather than cut with scissors, and get the skin underneath checked. Prevent it by drying the beard and feet after drinks and walks, keeping the beard trimmed, and brushing furnishings out to the skin several times a week.

conditions.name: Degenerative myelopathy
conditions.breedNote: The SOD1 variant behind DM appears in many breeds, but Giant Schnauzers were not among the 222 breeds in the largest published survey.
signs: back end slowly getting weaker over months
scuffing and wearing down her back nails
knuckling that she doesn't bother to correct
back legs cross over when she turns
wobbly but doesn't seem to be in any pain
struggles to get up off the floor
one back leg noticeably worse than the other at first
tail hangs limp and moves less
conditions.whatToDo: Book a vet exam — DM is a diagnosis of exclusion, so painless slow hind-limb weakness still needs imaging to rule out a disc, wobbler syndrome or a tumour first. A cheek-swab SOD1 test shows risk only and cannot confirm the disease.

conditions.name: Diabetes mellitus
conditions.breedNote: Miniature Schnauzers are strongly over-represented but that risk does not carry across to Giant Schnauzers. Entire bitches are at higher risk than males because of season-related insulin resistance.
signs: drinking and weeing a lot
wetting indoors or overnight
hungry all the time but losing weight
sticky patches where she has weed
cloudy eyes or bumping into things
coat looking poor and dull
sweet or nail-varnish smell on the breath
suddenly off her food and vomiting
sudden blindness
conditions.whatToDo: Book blood and urine glucose testing. Caught early this is manageable with twice-daily insulin and a fixed feeding routine. If she goes off food, starts vomiting or smells of acetone, treat it as an emergency — that suggests ketoacidosis.

conditions.name: Dry eye
signs: thick yellow or greenish gunk in the corner
sticky discharge that keeps coming back
eye looks dull instead of glossy
red and irritated whites
blinking or squinting a lot
brown staining creeping across the eye
keeps getting eye infections
eyelids stuck together in the morning
conditions.whatToDo: Ask for a Schirmer tear test — it takes a minute and is the only way to confirm it. Repeated goopy eyes treated as plain infection are very often untreated dry eye. Treatment is usually lifelong ciclosporin or tacrolimus drops.

conditions.name: Ear infection (otitis externa)
conditions.breedNote: Indirect: Giant Schnauzers have a documented elevated hypothyroidism risk, and endocrine disease is a recognised driver of repeat ear infections. Recurrence should prompt a hunt for a cause rather than another round of drops.
signs: shaking her head over and over
scratching or pawing at one ear
rubbing her ear along the couch or carpet
a bad or sour smell from the ear
brown, yellow or waxy gunk in the ear
the inside of the ear flap looks red or puffy
she flinches or yelps when you touch the ear
she tilts her head toward the sore side
the ear feels hot
one ear looks and smells different from the other
conditions.whatToDo: Book a vet visit within a few days and put nothing in the ear first — not leftover drops, not peroxide, not a cotton bud. The vet needs to see the canal and check the eardrum before choosing treatment. More than two or three infections a year warrants testing for allergies and thyroid disease.
sources: O'Neill DG et al., otitis externa in the UK — https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8422687/

conditions.name: Ear mites
signs: dry black crumbs like coffee grounds in the ear
furious, non-stop ear scratching
violent head shaking
scabs and scratch wounds around the ear and neck
both ears affected
other pets in the house scratching too
she scratches until the ear bleeds
hair worn away behind the ears
started soon after a shelter or kennel
conditions.whatToDo: Book a microscope check of the ear debris — mites need a parasiticide rather than a standard antibiotic drop, and the crumbly discharge is easily confused with yeast. All pets in the household usually need treating together.

conditions.name: Ectopic ureter
conditions.breedNote: Giant Schnauzers are not among the reported high-risk breeds; Labradors, Golden Retrievers, Huskies and Wheaten Terriers are.
signs: wet since she was a puppy
never been reliably house-trained
constant dribbling rather than puddles
damp back legs and belly all the time
urine-stained fur around her vulva
sore red skin from being always wet
she also squats and wees normally
keeps getting bladder infections
conditions.whatToDo: Ask about referral for imaging or cystoscopy — this is a plumbing fault present from birth and is usually correctable. Do not accept repeated antibiotic courses alone for a young dog who has leaked her whole life.

conditions.name: Elbow dysplasia
conditions.breedNote: OFA elbow statistics show 9.9% abnormal in 1,702 Giant Schnauzers, slightly BELOW the 12.0% all-breed average — the common claim that the breed is elbow-prone is not supported by OFA, though elbow screening remains a GSCA/CHIC requirement.
signs: limping on a front leg
lameness that gets worse after exercise
stiff front legs first thing in the morning
holds one front paw out at an odd angle
elbows held out away from the body
short choppy stride in front
reluctant to go down stairs
started limping as a young dog
swelling or thickening around the elbow
conditions.whatToDo: Front-leg lameness in a young large-breed dog should not be dismissed as a sprain — ask for elbow radiographs and a referral if the films are unclear. Catching it early widens the surgical options and slows the arthritis that follows.

conditions.name: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency (EPI)
conditions.breedNote: Documented in German Shepherds, Rough Collies and Eurasiers; no elevated risk documented in Giant Schnauzers.
signs: always hungry but losing weight
huge volumes of loose pale stool
greasy yellow poo
ravenous appetite
eating her own poo
very smelly gas
ribs showing despite eating well
dull greasy coat
conditions.whatToDo: Ask for a fasted serum TLI test plus B12 and folate — a simple blood test, and the diagnosis is easily missed. Treatment is lifelong enzyme replacement with every meal.

conditions.name: False (phantom) pregnancy
signs: milk or clear fluid from her teats when she isn't pregnant
swollen teats about four to nine weeks after a season
nesting, digging up bedding, hiding in corners
carrying a toy around and guarding it
off her food and a bit flat
restless, whiny or unusually clingy
slightly rounder tummy
licking her own teats constantly
conditions.whatToDo: Most cases settle within two to three weeks. Stop her licking the teats, do not milk them out, and leave the area alone. See a vet if she is genuinely ill, the glands are hot, hard or painful, or the behaviour is distressing her.

conditions.name: Fleas and flea allergy dermatitis
signs: itchy all the time
black pepper specks in the coat
specks that turn red when wet
chewing at the base of the tail
hair loss over the rump and back legs
red bumps and scabs on the belly
restless, can't settle
tiny fast bugs in the fur
pale gums in a small puppy
conditions.whatToDo: Use a vet-recommended product labelled for her age and weight, and treat every pet in the house plus bedding and carpets for at least three months. Ask the vet to check for tapeworm and, in a heavily infested puppy, anaemia.

conditions.name: Food allergy and adverse food reaction
signs: itchy skin and loose stool together
chewing her paws
recurring ear infections
soft stool for days
more than three poos a day
vomiting after certain foods
gassy and gurgling
red itchy belly
bottom scooting
conditions.whatToDo: Diagnosis is a strict 8-12 week elimination diet trial on a vet-prescribed novel-protein or hydrolysed diet with zero treats, chews or flavoured medications, then rechallenge. Blood, saliva and hair allergy tests do not diagnose food allergy.

conditions.name: Giardia
conditions.breedNote: In a Giant Schnauzer puppy, diarrhoea and poor growth persisting after parasites are cleared should prompt a B12 check.
signs: greasy soft poop
really foul smelling diarrhoea
pale or light coloured stool
mucus in the poop
diarrhoea comes and goes for weeks
gassy and rumbly belly
not gaining weight despite eating
still playful but loose stools
started after daycare, boarding or a puddle
conditions.whatToDo: Bring a fresh stool sample and mention any kennel, dog park or standing water exposure; diagnosis often needs a specific giardia antigen test rather than a routine float. Bathe the rear and clean bedding during treatment.

conditions.name: Gum disease
conditions.breedNote: Giant breeds are at lower risk than toy breeds. Published Miniature Schnauzer findings do not transfer to Giant Schnauzers.
signs: bad breath
red gum line
gums bleed when brushing
brown or yellow crust on the teeth
receding gums
loose or wobbly tooth
chewing on one side
dropping food
drooling more than usual
pus at the gum line
conditions.whatToDo: Book a dental exam — gingivitis is reversible but periodontitis under the gum line needs an anaesthetic cleaning with dental x-rays, since visible tartar shows only part of the problem. At home, brush daily with dog toothpaste, never human toothpaste.

conditions.name: Heart murmur and valve disease
conditions.breedNote: Degenerative mitral valve disease is mainly a small-breed problem. In a giant breed a new murmur more often points to DCM, subaortic stenosis or anaemia, so it should not be dismissed as 'just a murmur'.
signs: vet heard a murmur
tiring sooner than she used to
coughing on and off
breathing faster while asleep
fainted during excitement or exercise
gums slow to pink up when pressed
less keen on stairs or the car
quieter than usual for weeks
conditions.whatToDo: Ask for an echocardiogram to find out what the murmur actually is and how large her heart chambers are. Murmur grade alone is a poor guide to severity.

conditions.name: Heartworm disease
signs: soft persistent cough
tires out on short walks
breathing hard after mild activity
won't play like she used to
losing weight and muscle
swollen belly
fainting or collapse
coughing up blood
pale or bluish gums
missed a month of prevention
conditions.whatToDo: Keep her on year-round prevention and test yearly. If doses were missed or signs are showing, book a heartworm test before restarting a preventive. Collapse, blue gums or coughing blood is an emergency.

conditions.name: Hip dysplasia
conditions.breedNote: OFA hip statistics list the Giant Schnauzer at 17.5% dysplastic across 5,903 evaluations, above the 14.2% all-breed average, with only 11.9% graded Excellent. Hip screening is a GSCA/CHIC requirement.
signs: bunny hopping with both back legs
slow and stiff getting up from her bed
struggling with stairs
won't jump into the car anymore
swaying or wobbling in the back end
a clicking sound from the hips
sits with her legs flopped out to one side
stiff and sore the day after a long walk
flinches or yelps when you touch her hips
conditions.whatToDo: Ask about sedated hip radiographs graded by OFA or PennHIP, and keep her lean — body weight is the single biggest factor you control. Even established hip arthritis responds well to weight management, controlled exercise and modern pain medication.

conditions.name: Hypothyroidism and autoimmune thyroiditis
conditions.breedNote: Confirmed in the breed: of 236 Giant Schnauzers screened, 7.2% were already hypothyroid and a further 10.0% had raised thyroid autoantibodies, with a DLA risk haplotype identified. OFA thyroid testing is a CHIC requirement for the breed.
signs: putting on weight without eating more
slowed right down, sleeping more
coat gone dull, dry and thin
bald patches on the flanks or tail
seeking out warm spots, feels the cold
dark, thickened or greasy flaky skin
ear and skin infections that keep coming back
a droopy, sad-looking face
seasons stopped or irregular
conditions.whatToDo: Ask for a full thyroid panel with free T4, TSH and thyroglobulin autoantibodies — a total T4 alone misses early autoimmune cases. Mention the breed. Do not start any thyroid supplement before testing. Treatment is an inexpensive daily tablet and most dogs visibly improve within weeks.
sources: Ferm et al., J Small Anim Pract 2009 — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19320811/
Wilbe et al., Tissue Antigens 2010 — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20210920/

conditions.name: Kennel cough
signs: sudden honking cough
coughing then retching or gagging
sounds like something stuck in her throat
cough gets worse when the lead pulls on her neck
clear runny nose or sneezing
started a few days after boarding, daycare or the groomer
still eating and bright but coughing all night
low fever or a bit tired
other dogs she was with are coughing too
conditions.whatToDo: Book a vet visit and keep her away from other dogs — this spreads easily and she may shed for weeks. Go in the same day if she gets a high fever, stops eating, breathes fast or hard at rest, or the cough turns wet, which suggests pneumonia.

conditions.name: Lump in her mammary chain
conditions.breedNote: No confirmed Giant Schnauzer risk in the large insurance datasets. One small single-centre study flagged the breed and has not been replicated.
signs: pea-sized or bigger lump in one of her teat lines
several lumps along her belly at once
a lump that has grown noticeably in a few weeks
hard lump stuck down to the skin or body wall
red, hot, swollen gland
ulcerated or weeping skin over a lump
bloody or yellow fluid from one teat
swollen back leg near the lump
conditions.whatToDo: Any lump in the mammary chain of an entire bitch needs an appointment rather than watchful waiting — roughly half of canine mammary tumours are malignant, and size at removal strongly affects outcome. Run your hands along both teat lines monthly, especially after each season.

conditions.name: Lump or growth in the mouth
conditions.breedNote: No documented Giant Schnauzer predisposition to oral tumours. The breed's reported cancer risk concerns the toes, not the mouth.
signs: lump or bump on the gum
cauliflower-like warts on the lips or gums
swelling on one side of the face
bleeding from the mouth
bad breath that keeps getting worse
drooling, sometimes blood-tinged
dropping food or eating on one side
a tooth pushed out of place
loose tooth with no tartar around it
losing weight while still interested in food
conditions.whatToDo: Have any mouth lump examined rather than watched — appearance alone cannot tell a harmless growth from a malignant one, and a biopsy settles it. In young puppies, clustered wart-like growths are often viral papillomas that regress on their own.

conditions.name: Mange (sarcoptic and demodectic)
signs: frantic nonstop scratching
crusty scabby ear edges
bald patches around the eyes and mouth
thinning hair on elbows and hocks
red angry skin
thick greasy smelly skin
hair loss without much itching
sores from chewing herself raw
people in the house itchy too
scratches when you rub the ear tip
conditions.whatToDo: Ask for skin scrapings — intensely itchy sarcoptic mange is contagious to people while demodex usually is not, and the two are treated differently. Do not use over-the-counter dips on a puppy.

conditions.name: Mast cell tumour
conditions.breedNote: Not a documented Giant Schnauzer risk — Bulldog types and Retrievers carry the high odds.
signs: a lump that changes size
lump that goes red and angry then calms
raised pink lump on the skin
lump she keeps licking
soft lump that feels like a fatty lump
swelling that flares after being touched
lump that suddenly got bigger overnight
vomiting alongside a skin lump
conditions.whatToDo: Get any lump that changes size, reddens or flares needle-sampled — mast cell tumours mimic harmless fatty lumps and cannot be identified by feel. Avoid squeezing or repeatedly prodding it, which can trigger a histamine flare.

conditions.name: Nail bed cancer (digital squamous cell carcinoma)
conditions.breedNote: The strongest breed link of any condition here. In a review of 278,812 canine biopsies the Giant Schnauzer had the highest odds ratio of any dog for subungual SCC, at 56.7, with a schnauzer-specific KITLG risk marker.
signs: swollen painful toe
a nail that fell off
cracked, split or deformed nail
bleeding or oozing around one nail
licking or chewing one toe constantly
limping on one foot
toe looks red and lumpy
nail keeps growing back wrong
toe infection that won't clear up with antibiotics
a second toe does the same thing months later
conditions.whatToDo: In this breed a nail that splits, falls off, bleeds or leaves a swollen toe needs an x-ray of the toe and a biopsy, not another course of antibiotics. Say the words 'digital squamous cell carcinoma' to your vet — amputating the toe early is usually curative.
sources: Chiu et al., Can Vet J 2022 — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36325409/
Digital SCC in Giant, Standard and Miniature Schnauzers, Animals 2023 — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10295616/
KITLG variations in Schnauzer breeds, Vet Sci 2023 — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9966798/

conditions.name: Osteochondritis dissecans (OCD)
conditions.breedNote: A disorder of medium, large and rapidly growing dogs. The Giant Schnauzer does not appear in OFA's shoulder OCD breed table, so the risk comes from her size and growth rate rather than the breed.
signs: limp in one front leg between four and eight months old
lameness that gets worse after play, not better
shoulder sore when you reach the leg forward
muscle over the shoulder blade looks smaller on one side
won't bear full weight on one leg
stiff after resting following a big play session
limping that started with no injury you saw
cries out when the joint is flexed
conditions.whatToDo: Get radiographs of the sore joint — OCD in a fast-growing puppy usually needs arthroscopic or surgical treatment rather than rest alone. Stop forced exercise and check she is on a large- or giant-breed growth diet, since rapid growth and over-nutrition contribute.

conditions.name: Osteosarcoma (bone cancer)
conditions.breedNote: Risk tracks body size rather than this breed specifically: dogs over 40 kg had 45 times the odds of dogs under 10 kg, but Giant Schnauzers were not named among the top-risk breeds.
signs: limping that won't settle
limp that got worse over weeks
firm swelling on a leg
hard lump just above the wrist
yelping when the leg is touched
not wanting to jump in the car
leg gave way suddenly
limping that painkillers only half fix
conditions.whatToDo: Any limp in a big dog lasting more than two weeks, or any firm swelling on a limb, needs an x-ray rather than another course of rest and painkillers. If the leg gives way suddenly treat it as urgent — weakened bone can fracture.
sources: Edmunds et al., Canine Med Genet 2021 — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33750475/

conditions.name: Panosteitis (growing pains)
conditions.breedNote: Affects young, rapidly growing large- and giant-breed dogs, which is exactly her category. There is no registry or breed-specific prevalence figure.
signs: limping that moves between legs week to week
sudden limp with no injury you saw
yelps when you squeeze the long bone of a leg
off her food and a bit feverish with the limp
flat and sleepy for a few days at a time
lameness that comes and goes in waves
worse after a long walk or hard play
first showed up between five and eighteen months
conditions.whatToDo: See your vet to confirm it is pano and not something needing surgery — diagnosis rests on squeezing the long bones and on radiographs. It is self-limiting and she will outgrow it, but she needs pain relief and rest during flare-ups.

conditions.name: Progressive retinal atrophy (PRA-N)
conditions.breedNote: The breed's own PRA form is PRA-N (NECAP1), first described in Giant Schnauzers — NOT prcd-PRA, which has no published case series in this breed. Evidence is only three affected dogs from one litter, and the variant is not yet confirmed pathogenic. The CHIC eye requirement is an annual CAER exam by an ophthalmologist, not a DNA test.
signs: bumping into things at dusk
won't go down stairs in the dark
nervous or clingy at night
eyes shine back very brightly
pupils look wide open all the time
startles when you walk up to her
can't find a treat dropped on the floor
fine in daylight, lost at night
conditions.whatToDo: Book a board-certified veterinary ophthalmologist for a full retinal exam — PRA is painless and easy to miss until vision is far gone. There is no cure, so the work is confirming it, ruling out treatable causes of night blindness, and keeping furniture and routines predictable.

conditions.name: Puppy vaginitis
signs: sticky white or yellow discharge from her vulva
