crusty gunk in the hair around her private parts
licking her private parts a lot
a faint smell from her back end
otherwise completely well, eating and playing normally
scooting her bottom along the floor
reddened skin folds around the vulva
no fever and no straining to wee
conditions.whatToDo: Get one vet check to rule out a urine infection, a recessed vulva and a foreign body, then usually just keep the area clean with plain water or unscented wipes. It normally resolves after her first season.

conditions.name: Recognising pain
signs: hiding and doesn't want to be touched
hunched back or a tucked-up belly
won't jump into the car or go up stairs
slow to get up after lying down
panting at rest when it isn't hot
eating less or dropping food
licking or chewing one spot over and over
grumbles or snaps when handled in one area
restless, keeps changing position
trembling or shaking
conditions.whatToDo: Treat any sudden change in posture, appetite, willingness to move or tolerance of handling as possible pain and book a vet. Never give human painkillers — ibuprofen, paracetamol and aspirin are toxic to dogs. A stoic dog who is still eating and wagging can be in significant pain.

conditions.name: Retained baby teeth
conditions.breedNote: Most often reported in toy and flat-faced breeds; Giant Schnauzers have no documented excess risk, but any puppy can be affected.
signs: two teeth in one spot
two rows of teeth
baby tooth still there at 6-7 months
adult canine coming in beside a baby canine
crowded or crooked front teeth
food packing between teeth
bad breath in a young puppy
red puffy gum around one tooth
conditions.whatToDo: If a baby tooth and its adult replacement are both present at once, book a vet exam rather than waiting. Persistent teeth are usually extracted promptly because crowding traps plaque and can push the adult tooth out of position.

conditions.name: Ringworm
signs: round bald patch with flaky edges
crusty scaly spots on her face
broken stubbly hairs
hair loss on her muzzle or ears
brittle crumbly claws
patches spreading slowly
not always itchy
someone in the house has a ring-shaped rash
spots after time in a kennel or shelter
conditions.whatToDo: See a vet for a fungal culture or PCR before treating — ringworm needs weeks of systemic plus topical antifungal therapy and mimics several other conditions. It is contagious to people, so wear gloves and ask about decontaminating bedding and grooming tools.

conditions.name: Roundworms
signs: pot-bellied puppy
white spaghetti-like worms in poop
worms in vomit
dull rough coat
not growing well
soft or mucousy stool
poor appetite but round belly
coughing in a young puppy
thin over the ribs
conditions.whatToDo: Bring a fresh stool sample and follow the full deworming series rather than a single dose — most puppies are born already infected. Pick up stool promptly and wash hands, because roundworm eggs can infect people.

conditions.name: Skin infection (pyoderma and yeast)
conditions.breedNote: Risk here is coat-driven rather than genetic: a dense double coat, beard and leg furnishings hold moisture against skin.
signs: pimples and scabs along her back
circular flaky bald patches
crusty bumps you feel when brushing
musty or corn-chip smell
greasy feeling coat
skin gone thick and grey between her back legs
red inflamed skin between her toes
brown waxy ear discharge
rust-brown stain on her leg hair from licking
conditions.whatToDo: See a vet for skin cytology — bacteria and yeast look similar but need different drugs, and both are almost always secondary to allergy, parasites or a hormonal problem. Expect medicated shampoo plus treatment of the underlying cause, and do not stop antibiotics early.

conditions.name: Tapeworms
signs: rice grains near the tail
white moving segments in poop
sesame seed things in the bed
scooting on the carpet
licking or biting at the rear
fleas or flea dirt in the coat
occasional loose stool
otherwise bright and normal
conditions.whatToDo: Tapeworm needs praziquantel, which most general puppy wormers and many monthly preventives do not cover — call the vet rather than reusing a leftover product. Treat fleas at the same time or she will simply be reinfected.

conditions.name: Urethral sphincter mechanism incompetence (leaking urine)
conditions.breedNote: Giant Schnauzers are named among the breeds over-represented for sphincter mechanism incompetence in the USA, alongside Dobermans. This is incontinence, not infection — a distinction often muddled.
signs: wet patch where she slept
dribbling urine without knowing it
damp fur between her back legs
smells faintly of urine
licking herself a lot down there
leaks when she is excited or relaxed
worse after she was spayed
she still squats and wees normally otherwise
red or sore skin around her vulva
conditions.whatToDo: Book a routine vet visit and take a fresh morning urine sample so infection and other causes are ruled out first. This is treatable with medication in most dogs, so it is worth investigating rather than managing with towels.
sources: ACVIM Consensus Statement on Urinary Incontinence in Dogs, JVIM 2024 — https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/jvim.16975

conditions.name: Urinary tract infection
conditions.breedNote: No breed predisposition is documented for Giant Schnauzers. Female dogs in general get UTIs more often than males.
signs: squatting again and again
only a few drops each time
blood in her wee
straining and it seems to hurt
asking to go out much more often
accidents in the house from a clean dog
licking herself a lot
wee smells strong or cloudy
seems a bit off in herself
conditions.whatToDo: Get her seen within a day or two with a fresh mid-stream urine sample. Antibiotics should be chosen on a urine culture where possible, never guessed or left over from a previous course.

conditions.name: Whipworms
signs: diarrhoea with fresh blood
slimy mucus on the poop
straining to poop
urgent frequent poops
diarrhoea that keeps coming back
losing weight slowly
gassy and gurgly
dull coat and low energy
conditions.whatToDo: Ask for a faecal test, and tell the vet if it comes back negative but signs persist — whipworm eggs shed intermittently and are easily missed. Treatment runs over about three months, and eggs survive years in soil.

conditions.name: Wobbler syndrome
conditions.breedNote: A large- and giant-breed disease, but the breeds named in the literature are Doberman, Great Dane, Mastiff and Rottweiler. Giant Schnauzers are not on that list — this is size-based inference only.
signs: wobbly, drunk-looking back end
back legs cross over each other when she turns
long floaty stride behind, short choppy stride in front
scuffing her nails on the ground
worn-down toenails on the back feet
holds her neck low and stiff
yelps or flinches when her neck is touched
won't turn her head to take a treat
legs slide out from under her on smooth floors
conditions.whatToDo: Switch to a chest harness instead of a neck collar, keep her off stairs and slippery floors, and book a vet exam — confirming it needs MRI and usually a neurologist. Go in urgently if she goes down and cannot get up.
sources: da Costa RC, Vet Clin North Am 2010 — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20732597/

conditions.name: Dietary indiscretion (she ate something she shouldn't)
signs: vomiting after raiding the bin
sudden diarrhoea overnight
eating grass and vomiting
gurgling noisy stomach
passing gas and mucus
off her food for a day
yellow or foamy vomit
straining with soft stool
seems tired but still drinking
conditions.whatToDo: Withhold food for a few hours (never water), then offer small bland meals and watch for 24-48 hours. Call the vet sooner for repeated vomiting, blood, a bloated or painful belly, unproductive retching, or if she cannot keep water down.

conditions.name: Her normal vital signs
conditions.breedNote: As a large breed her resting heart rate normally sits toward the lower end of the range.
signs: breathing more than 35 breaths a minute while fully asleep
resting breathing rate has climbed above her usual number
heart rate over 180 or under 60 beats a minute
pulse in the inner thigh feels weak or you can't find it
pulse feels irregular or skips
temperature over 103F (39.4C)
temperature under 99F (37.2C) and she feels cold
panting hard when it isn't hot and she hasn't exercised
conditions.whatToDo: Learn her normal numbers while she is well and write them down: temperature 101-102.5F (38.3-39.2C), heart rate 70-120 bpm counted at the femoral pulse in the groin, sleeping breathing rate 18-34 a minute. A change from her own normal is far more useful than any textbook range.

conditions.name: Her season (what is normal)
conditions.breedNote: Large and giant breeds often have a late first season, commonly around 12 to 24 months, and may cycle only once a year rather than twice.
signs: swollen vulva a few days before any blood appears
bloody discharge that fades to watery pink
licking herself more than usual
male dogs suddenly very interested in her
weeing little and often on walks
clingy, restless or moody for a couple of weeks
flagging her tail to one side when touched near her back end
roughly two to three weeks start to finish
conditions.whatToDo: Write down the first day you see swelling or blood — that date is what lets a vet judge whether a later illness could be pyometra or a phantom pregnancy. Keep her on lead and away from entire males for the whole season and about a week beyond it.

conditions.name: Normal teething
signs: chewing everything in sight
tiny tooth found on the floor
small spots of blood on toys
pink-tinged drool
gums look red where a tooth is coming in
eating a little slower for a day or two
swallowed a baby tooth
gaps in the front teeth
sore mouth around 4-6 months
conditions.whatToDo: Baby teeth are normally lost from about 3 to 6 months and swallowed teeth are harmless. Offer soft flexible chew toys. Get it checked if she stops eating, or if a baby tooth is still there once the adult tooth beside it has erupted.

conditions.name: Osteoarthritis
conditions.breedNote: Her main arthritis driver is over-represented in the breed: OFA records 17.5% hip dysplasia in Giant Schnauzers against 14.2% across all breeds, and developmental joint disease predisposes to early arthritis.
signs: stiff for the first few minutes after a nap
slower on walks than she used to be
hesitates at the bottom of the stairs
needs a run-up or help to get in the car
sleeps more and plays less
licking one joint over and over
grumpy when touched or brushed over the hips
slipping on smooth floors
muscle loss over her back end
worse in cold or damp weather
conditions.whatToDo: Book an arthritis check rather than writing it off as age. Keeping her lean is the single most effective thing, alongside prescription pain relief, controlled exercise and traction on slippery floors.

conditions.name: Seasonal flank alopecia
conditions.breedNote: Schnauzers appear on the predisposed-breed list, though most sources do not specify which variety.
signs: bald patches on both flanks
dark grey or black skin where the hair went
hair loss with sharp clean edges
same patches every autumn
hair grows back in spring
skin looks normal, just bare
not itchy at all
she seems perfectly well otherwise
conditions.whatToDo: Mention it at a routine visit so hypothyroidism, Cushing's and other hair-loss causes can be ruled out. It is cosmetic and often self-resolving; no treatment is required.
